```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 96)
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

gambitR3D plays one experimental profile, `experimental-v0.1`. It is a
transparent project convention: the basic board arrangement follows a supplied
concept, and every question the concept leaves open is answered by an explicit,
recorded decision. It is not an official rulebook of any published game.

```{r}
prof <- gambitR3D::g3_rules_profile()
prof
# Every decision, and whether it comes from the concept or is a proposed resolution.
prof$decisions[, c("id", "topic", "origin")]
```

The rules hash is computed from the resolved semantics only. Changing any rule
changes the hash, and games recorded under one hash cannot be replayed under
another. Rewording an explanation does not change it.

## Boards and physical squares

There are three fixed 4×4 boards and four movable 2×2 platforms: 64 physical
squares in all. Each square has a permanent id `board:u:v`, with zero-based
local column `u` and row `v`. The board's position decides which projected file
(`a`–`f`) and rank (`0`–`9`) a square stands on.

| Board | Files | Ranks |
|---|---|---|
| W (White's main board) | b–e | 1–4 |
| N (Neutral, the middle board) | b–e | 3–6 |
| B (Black's main board) | b–e | 5–8 |

W and N share eight projected coordinates (b–e, ranks 3–4), and N and B share
eight more (b–e, ranks 5–6). Those coordinates exist twice, as two different
physical squares. Selecting `b4` on W is never the same as selecting `b4` on N.

```{r}
st <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()$state
st
```

The four platforms are `WQ`, `WK`, `BQ` and `BK`. These names are persistent
identities, not owners: a platform belongs to whoever has the single piece on it.
At the start they stand on files a–b (`WQ`, `BQ`) and e–f (`WK`, `BK`), at the
outer ends of W and B.

## Display is not geometry

The 3D view separates the boards so that White's and Black's main boards are
exactly two square-widths apart, with Neutral centred between them, shown
highest or lowest. That spacing exists only on screen. It adds no ranks and
changes no move: legal actions, keys and every analysis are identical whatever
the display settings. The diagrams below show the plan view used by the 3D
scene (square centres at `x = file - 2.5`, `z = 4.5 - rank + offset`, with
offsets +1 for W, 0 for N, -1 for B) and, for comparison, the logical
projection without offsets, where W/N and N/B overlap.

```{r plan-view, eval = has_ggplot, fig.alt = "Plan view of the seven boards in display spacing and in the logical projection"}
tabs <- gambitR3D:::.g3_tables()
core <- gambitR3D:::.g3_core(st, tabs)
co <- gambitR3D:::.g3_square_coords(core$dock, core$orient, tabs)
board <- tabs$board_ids[tabs$sq_board]
parent <- ifelse(board %in% c("W", "N", "B"), board,
                 substr(tabs$dock_ids[core$dock[match(board, c("WQ", "WK", "BQ", "BK"))]], 1, 1))
offset <- c(W = 1, N = 0, B = -1)[parent]
squares <- rbind(
  data.frame(view = "Display spacing (3D scene, plan view)", board = board,
             x = co$file - 2.5, z = 4.5 - co$rank + offset),
  data.frame(view = "Logical projection (no display offsets)", board = board,
             x = co$file - 2.5, z = 4.5 - co$rank)
)
squares$label <- paste0(c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f")[co$file + 1], co$rank)
# In display spacing one row of N lies over one row of W and of B in plan
# view: nudge the labels apart (N below, others above) so both stay legible.
disp <- squares$view == squares$view[1]
squares$label_z <- squares$z + ifelse(disp, ifelse(squares$board == "N", -0.22, 0.22), 0)
ggplot2::ggplot(squares, ggplot2::aes(x, z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(ggplot2::aes(fill = board), width = 0.94, height = 0.94, alpha = 0.55) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(y = label_z, label = label), size = 2.2) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~view) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::coord_equal() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x (files)", y = "z (towards White)", fill = "Board") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

In display spacing the facing edges of W (at z = +1) and B (at z = -1) are two
units apart. Neutral overlaps one rendered row of each outer board in plan view;
in the logical projection the overlap is the two shared ranks.

## Moving pieces

Moves are measured in projected files and ranks. A piece may land on any
existing physical square that fits its pattern, empty or holding an enemy; only
that exact occupant is captured. Moving to the same projected coordinate on
another board is not a move.

Sliding pieces are blocked by any piece on any board standing on a coordinate
they cross (decision D07). Rays may pass coordinates that have no square, but
cannot end there. Pieces on other boards at the starting coordinate do not block.

```{r}
pieces <- data.frame(
  id = c("wR", "wK", "bP", "bK"), type = c("R", "K", "P", "K"),
  color = c("white", "white", "black", "black"),
  square_id = c("W:0:0", "WK:0:0", "N:0:0", "B:3:3")
)
pos <- gambitR3D::g3_setup_position(pieces)
acts <- gambitR3D::g3_legal_actions(pos)
# The rook reaches W:b3 and captures on N:b3, but the pawn on N:b3 blocks
# the coordinate b3, so W:b4 is out of reach although W itself is empty.
acts$label[acts$piece_id == "wR"]
```

Knights jump (1, 2) in projected coordinates; kings step one coordinate in any
direction. Two kings on the same projected coordinate on different boards are
not adjacent and do not attack each other (D08).

Pawns move one rank forward to an empty square, capture one file aside and one
rank forward, and an unmoved pawn may step two ranks if no piece on any board
stands on the crossed coordinate (D09). White moves towards rank 9, Black
towards rank 0; a platform's rotation never changes that.

## Moving platforms

A platform can move when it carries exactly one piece, belonging to the player
to act (D05). It goes to an adjacent free dock, either keeping its orientation
or turned by 180°. The pieces stay on their physical squares; their projected
coordinates change with the platform.

```{r}
docks <- prof$semantics$dock_adjacency
data.frame(dock = names(docks), neighbours = vapply(docks, function(x) paste(unlist(x), collapse = ", "), ""))
```

The adjacency graph (D04) connects, on one board, the corners on the same pin
rank or pin file, and between W–N and N–B the same-side docks whose pin ranks are
at most two apart. W and B are never directly connected. It is an inferred
graph, consistent with the concept's examples, not the only possible reading.

Transport consumes rights: the carried piece counts as moved, a carried king or
rook loses castling, a carried pawn loses its double step and resets the
100-ply counter (D10). A platform carrying the king may leave check if the
destination is safe; the path in between means nothing.

## Special actions

- **Promotion (D11)** happens on arrival: White on rank 8 of B or rank 9 of a
  platform docked at a B high dock; Black on rank 1 of W or rank 0 of a platform
  at a W low dock. A platform action that brings its pawn there includes the
  promotion choice. Nothing promotes passively.
- **En passant (D12)** follows only an individual pawn double step; the capturing
  pawn may land on any empty square at the crossed coordinate.
- **Castling (D13, D14)** is a compound action after the player's first turn,
  with the original king and rook on their home squares and home docks. King
  side swaps king and rook on the king platform; queen side moves the king to
  b0/b9 and the rook to e0/e9, needs b0/b9 empty and nothing on the projected d
  and c coordinates, and probes d, c and b for attacks even where no square
  exists.

## End of the game

Checkmate and stalemate count platform actions as possible escapes. Automatic
draws are the third repetition, 100 plies without a capture or pawn action, and
bare kings (D16). They are decided in the order checkmate, stalemate,
repetition, 100-ply limit, bare kings (D17). A computer simulation that stops at
a ply limit is *truncated*, never a draw.

```{r}
mate <- gambitR3D::g3_setup_position(data.frame(
  id = c("wK", "bN", "bR1", "bR2", "bB", "bK"),
  type = c("K", "N", "R", "R", "B", "K"),
  color = c("white", rep("black", 5)),
  square_id = c("WK:0:0", "W:2:1", "N:3:3", "BK:1:1", "N:0:0", "B:0:3")
))
# White's king is attacked; no king step and no platform destination is safe.
mate$outcome
```
